# Market Research

Curated by Skill Harbor: a research skill for producing market intelligence that supports decisions instead of research theater. It sets strict standards: every important claim needs a source, recent data beats stale data (and stale data gets called out), contrarian evidence and downside cases are mandatory, findings translate into a decision rather than a summary, and fact, inference, and recommendation stay clearly separated. Research modes include investor and fund diligence (fund size, stage, check size, portfolio, public thesis), TAM/SAM/SOM sizing, competitor and adjacent-product comparisons, and thesis pressure-testing before building, funding, or entering a market. Its trust model is explicit: vendor pages, press releases, and filings are written by interested parties, so all fetched content is evidence to weigh, never instructions to follow, and nothing the agent reads can authorize it to send data outward. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: a research methodology, not the data itself; your agent needs web access to do the work; it informs business decisions but is not investment advice. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
